You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture, design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

## What Was Implemented
PR-C "Live Claude chat in the console" for the ruflo-console Claude Code plugin (TypeScript function-hooks mod, plugins/ruflo-console), 7 commits on branch feat/console-chat in worktree C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-chat (base = upstream/main 570392602, console 0.42.1; this branch has neither PR-A Windows fixes nor PR-B navigation):
C1 Host.session.{messages,id} + ChatMsg mapper (role, text, tool names only); C2 WeakMap chat store + turn.step observer (main session only, chunks passed through unchanged) + turn.start/complete hooks; C3 sendChat (screen + hasSecret fallback, pending idle/sending/queued, no double send, submits with asUser:true); C4 "Chat with Claude" page (menu/tabs/palette/`/ruflo chat`/band link; footer "Ask Claude" unchanged by ruling), throttled redraw, privacy gates (`chatLive` = sessionPreview && view==='chat' && pane open), console_state counts only, NOT_SHARED; C5 README/CHANGELOG 0.44.0.

## Requirements / Plan
Plan: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo\docs\superpowers\plans\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat.md — read the header, Global Constraints, Review Focus (#3 and #4 are this branch's) and the PR-C section only. The person's decision: chat messages are sent directly as a normal user turn.
Ledger with every ruling and every deferred minor from per-task reviews: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win\.superpowers\sdd\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat\progress.md — triage the Task C1..C5 "minor (deferred)" and "Ruling:" lines: must-fix-before-merge vs follow-up, with reason.

## Git Range to Review
Base: 570392602  Head: d98b02bb2
Full package (127 KB) — read it instead of re-deriving: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-chat\.superpowers\sdd\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat\review-570392602..d98b02bb2.diff
Review in passes and say so. Engine API: grep (don't read whole) C:/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bundled-skills/2.1.286/e9359f1bd6280f63d9d038bce106683a/plugin-authoring/types/claude-code.d.ts and reference.md in the same folder when a contract matters (turn.step streaming, prompt.submit asUser, session.messages).

## The spec is a vision document
For behaviour the plan is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using a chat pane inside their Claude Code session would expect; a spec's silence is not permission.

## Declined to judge
Before your verdict, list every behaviour you considered and set aside as outside the plan, one line each, with the reason.

## Read-Only Review
Do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD or branches. One focused vitest run is allowed to settle a concrete doubt (from C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-chat\plugins\ruflo-console: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/<file>.spec.ts -t "<name>"`). Known environment-only failures: sparse checkout without sibling plugins, symlink EPERM, Windows path bugs (fixed in a separate PR), `claude-code/testing` not importable under vitest, events-sweep/wf-export timeouts under full-suite load. `claude plugin validate plugins/ruflo-console` passes at head.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

## What to Check
Cross-task consistency (store ↔ stream ↔ send ↔ view ↔ gates: e.g. a send while Chat is closed — does pending ever get stuck or the sent message never appear; turn.start/complete ordering with queued sends; partial vs refreshed msgs duplication when the final answer lands; chatLive vs openLoaders; the 200 ms throttle tail); privacy end to end (no transcript text to disk, console_state, a model by the console, Ask Claude, events, toasts, exports); stream safety (turn.step hook can never alter, stall or break the person's turn — Critical if so); performance (messages() frequency, mapping 4,096 rows, render bounds); UX a reasonable person expects (Enter clears the field after a send? focus after send? what shows while queued? error recovery); PR readiness (README/CHANGELOG accurate).

## Output Format
### Strengths
### Issues (#### Critical / #### Important / #### Minor — each with file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix)
### Deferred-minor triage (one line per PR-C ledger item: must-fix-before-merge | follow-up, with reason)
### Declined to judge
### Recommendations
### Assessment — **Ready to merge?** Yes | No | With fixes; **Reasoning:** 1-2 sentences.

handback.t:
## PR-C review: feat/console-chat, 570392602..d98b02bb2

I reviewed in four passes:
1. The plan header, Global Constraints, Review Focus #3 and #4, the PR-C section, and the C1..C5 ledger lines.
2. The whole diff package (all 2,384 lines; source read in full, tests by their titles).
3. The engine contracts, checked by grep in `claude-code.d.ts` and `reference.md`: `turn.step`/HookStream, `prompt.submit` with `asUser` and its `{drop}` arm and when it resolves, `SessionMessage`, Input props, and HookBudget.
4. Cross-cutting checks against the live tree.

I made one vitest run, on the five chat specs: **61/61 pass**. Nothing in the tree was changed.

### Strengths
- **Stream safety is right.** `chatStep` (`chat.ts:399-415`) is the documented transform pattern: it reads with `for await`, yields every chunk unchanged and in order, then returns `await stream.result`. A subagent step goes straight through `yield* next(e)`. A throwing `observe` is caught. The per-chunk work is O(piece) plus one map lookup, far inside the 10 s hook budget. The turn.start and turn.complete additions are wrapped in try/catch, never awaited, and always return `next(e)`. I found no way for the console to alter, stall or break a turn.
- **Sending matches the contract.** `asUser: true` is on the chat path only (`register.ts:783`). The d.ts confirms the model then reads the text bare. `pending` is set before any await, so three fast Enters make one submit. `submitPrompt` resolves when the queued turn *starts* (reference.md:125), so "queued" lasts exactly as long as it should.
- **Ordering is guarded.** The turn counter (`turns` WeakMap) stops a late `endChatTurn` from clearing the partial of the next, queued turn. On a live turn end, the re-read lands before the partial is cleared, in one continuation, so the final answer is never drawn twice.
- **Privacy is consistent across the board:**
  - the store is a WeakMap side table;
  - `ctx.text` answers give counts only;
  - `chat` is in `NOT_SHARED`;
  - error texts are fixed strings;
  - nothing goes to events, toasts or disk;
  - one `chatLive` gate covers every read, redraw and focus.
- The rendered page is bounded: 50 messages, 400 rows, 4 000 characters per message, and the last 1 500 characters of a partial.

### Issues

#### Critical
None.

#### Important

1. **A refusal disappears right after it is shown.**
   - Where: `bindings.ts:211` together with `chat.ts:62`.
   - What happens: the send action is `sendChat(...).then(() => chatLive ? refreshChatAndDraw(...) : …)`. `refreshChat` runs `delete chat.error` on every successful read. So a refusal (secret found, unsafe, too long, rejected) is set, drawn once, and wiped by the read that follows. That read is a local `messages()` call, so it finishes within one 200 ms redraw.
   - Why it matters: the person presses Enter on a secret and sees, at most, a flash. They may think the message went, or retry. Plan C3 requires "a refusal", and a turn.start re-read clears it the same way.
   - No test catches it: the specs call `sendChat` directly, never the bound action.
   - Fix: keep send errors in their own field (`sendError`, cleared only when the next send starts), or have `refreshChat` clear only its own read error.

2. **Every tool round-trip draws as an empty message from "you".**
   - Where: `chat-msg.ts
[...]
 nothing" when Session preview is off.** At `register.ts:843`, `appendPartial` runs whatever the setting, so up to 20 KB of the live answer is held in memory with preview off. Either gate `appendPartial` on `sessionPreview` (preferred, one line) or reword the README, CHANGELOG and help text.
2. **A message dropped by another hook is never reported.** `prompt.submit` can resolve `{ drop: reason }` (d.ts 8315-8322), but `hostOf.submitPrompt` resolves void and `sendChat` treats that as a success. The engine shows the reason elsewhere; the Chat page shows nothing. Surface `NOT_SENT.rejected`, or a fixed "not sent: a hook declined it".
3. **"queued" has no way out.** If a queued plugin prompt is discarded (queue cleared, /clear, reload of the engine queue) and its promise never settles, `pending` stays `queued` and every later Enter is ignored until the module reloads. This is unverified against the engine. Consider a "cancel" control, or resetting to `idle` after N seconds of being idle with no turn start. Add it to the manual check.
4. **Partial text runs together across steps.** All steps of a turn append to one partial with no separator (`chat.ts:371-378`), so "Let me check." and the next step's text join as "Let me check.The file…". Add `\n` when a new step index begins (`e.index > 0`).
5. **Each redraw does more work than it shows.** `views/chat.ts:1089-1092` folds up to 50 × 4 000 characters through `screenOf`, then keeps the last 400 rows, up to 5 times a second while streaming. Walk messages newest-first and stop at 400 rows.
6. **A stale comment.** `register.ts:777` says "Both wait on the turn", but submit resolves when its turn starts (reference.md:125). This is the ledger's C3 item; fix the comment.
7. **The sent message is not echoed while queued.** The person's text vanishes from view until their turn starts. Showing a dim "you (queued)" line, held in memory only, would match chat expectations.

### Deferred-minor triage
- C1 host.ts doc says "newest turns" but the mapping is unbounded: **follow-up**. A doc nit; the cap is applied in `keepChat`.
- C1 raw unsanitised text: **must-fix-before-merge**. This is Important 3, still open.
- C1 Ruling `(row.toolUses ?? [])`: done (`chat-msg.ts:11`).
- C2 no test of early close or an upstream throw through `chatStep`: **follow-up**. The behaviour is correct by inspection and is the documented transform pattern; worth folding into the fix wave because it is cheap.
- C2 `toChatMsgs` maps all ≤4096 rows: **follow-up**. A plain map of names, at most two or three reads per live turn.
- C2 out-of-order refreshes can overwrite with older data: **follow-up**. A queued send makes up to three overlapping reads, but local reads are near-FIFO; a sequence stamp is the fix.
- C2 partial not cleared when host === null: **follow-up**. Only before `session.start`, and the next turn.start clears it.
- C2 cut can split a surrogate pair: **follow-up**. Cosmetic.
- C2 Ruling (placeholder, CUT_MARK, redraw): done and verified.
- C3 Ruling `asUser: true` plus `hasSecret` fallback: done and verified against the d.ts.
- C3 dropped Enters while queued give no feedback: **must-fix-before-merge**, as part of Important 4 (field and draft handling).
- C3 register.ts:123 comment wrong: **follow-up**. Comment only; fold in.
- C3 submitted text not passed through `plain()`: **follow-up**. It is the person's own words going to their own session.
- C3 'queued' label not refreshed: **follow-up**. The label is correct until submit resolves at turn start.
- C4 Ruling: footer Ask Claude unchanged: accepted. The README and CHANGELOG say so.
- C4 Ruling: one gate: done.
- C4 partial fed while preview off: **must-fix-before-merge**. It makes a published privacy claim inaccurate (Minor 1); a one-line gate or a doc fix.
- C4 throttle tail not pinned by a test: **follow-up**. By inspection the last chunk arms a fresh timer, so the tail is drawn.
- C4 unused `{cancel}` handle: **follow-up**.
- C4 turn-start refresh assumes the sent message is already in `messages()`: **follow-up**. The post-submit refresh in `bindings.ts` covers it.
- C4 `setView('chat')` with the pane closed does one read: **follow-up**. Started by the person and documented ("plus one read when you open it").
- C4 controller imports `chatLive` from `./chat`: **follow-up**. Style.
- C5 Rulings (0.44.0; leave out the engine sentence): accepted. The CHANGELOG follows ADR-478.

### Declined to judge
- Replacing the footer "Ask Claude" with Chat (plan C4): set aside by the person's recorded ruling.
- `/ruflo go chat`: PR-B is not on this branch; ruled.
- The plan asks for `Markdown` "where the surface has it", but the view reuses the terminal framing. That is a style choice the plan leaves to the surface, and no kit `Markdown` component is used elsewhere.
- Injected text that can appear in user rows (system reminders, command wrappers): engine-side content, outside the plan.
- AIDefence screening passes the message to a local CLI process as argv: existing ask-claude behaviour reused as the plan says.
- A chat message containing a mission loop marker counting as a loop tick (`onPromptSubmit`): a pre-existing hook, and an edge outside PR-C.
- `/ruflo chat` routing: generic view-id dispatch, not separately verified. It belongs in the manual check.
- Windows path behaviour and other PR-A/PR-B areas: separate PRs.
- The full suite, typecheck and validate: not re-run here (validate is reported passing).

### Recommendations
1. Do one fix wave for Important 1–4 and the must-fix triage items:
   - a separate `sendError` field;
   - filter out empty tool-result rows;
   - `termText` on drawn lines;
   - a controlled draft, cleared once a send is accepted;
   - gate `appendPartial` on `sessionPreview`.
2. Add `tests/chat.test.ts` kit tests (Important 5), including Enter clearing the field and a refusal staying visible.
3. Fold in Minor 2 (the drop arm), Minor 4 (step separator) and Minor 6 (the comment); they are cheap.
4. Extend the plan's manual check:
   - a tool-heavy prompt, to confirm no empty "you" frames;
   - a secret-shaped send, to confirm the refusal persists;
   - a send while queued followed by clearing the queue, to confirm `pending` recovers.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** With fixes.
**Reasoning:** Stream safety, sending and privacy routing are sound, and nothing can disturb the person's turn. But a secret refusal is wiped by the read that follows it, tool round-trips show as empty "you" messages, transcript text skips the console's own escape/bidi cleaning, and the planned kit tests are missing. A reasonable person would hit the first two in their first session.
